column1: # Per-assembly line-coverage floors.
# There is ONE profile now: `full` — corpora present, reference tools present,
# unfiltered. The `ci` profile and its rows were DELETED on 2026-09-04 together
# with GitHub Actions (see LOCAL_GATES.md). They described a corpus-less runner
# that no longer exists anywhere in this project, and keeping numbers for an
# environment nobody runs is how the 0.76 outage happened in the first place.
# The history is worth keeping even though the profile is gone, because the
# lesson outlives it:
#     ci    corpus-less runner, filtered           54.36%
#     dev machine w/ CI's filter (NOT a profile)   78.41%
#     full  corpora + mutool/gs/pdftocairo, all    87.49%
# Applying a filter locally does not reproduce an environment. The 24-point gap
# was tests that SKIP when a corpus is missing — they run, find nothing, and
# skip, so the local run looks like the remote one and measures 24 points high.
# If you ever reintroduce a second environment, give it its own profile and read
# its number FROM that environment, never from here.
# HOW FLOORS ARE CHOSEN
# ~2 points below the measured value: tight enough to catch a real regression,
# loose enough not to flap.
# THE RATCHET IS MECHANICAL, NOT ASPIRATIONAL (#909)
#     scripts/check-coverage-floor.sh <report> full <assembly> --update
# raises the floor when coverage improved materially, keeping ~2 points of
# headroom, and rewrites the `measured` column either way. Three rules, each
# enforced by scripts/test-check-coverage-floor.sh in t0:
#   * it NEVER lowers — a regression exits non-zero and leaves this file
#     untouched. A ratchet that rewrote the floor to match a drop would launder
#     exactly the regressions it exists to catch.
#   * it ignores marginal gains, so run-to-run wobble cannot tighten a floor.
#   * it keeps headroom, matching how the hand-chosen floors were set.
# Format:  profile <TAB> assembly <TAB> floor <TAB> measured <TAB> note
# `measured` is the observation the floor was derived from.
full
